game.name: SYNTHETIK: Legion Rising
game.short_description: SYNTHETIK is an unforgiving tactical shooter rogue-lite where freedom and experimentation is key. Fight in a world overrun by the Machine Legion and their Gods. Experience the next level in gun-play and dive into unparalleled build options and Android upgrades. Can you defeat the Heart of Armageddon?

other_scores.source: Metacritic critic reviews (3 individual, no Metascore)

commentary.label: Tier list Part 3 (2025)
commentary.summary: Synthetik is a slow, top-down shooter roguelike that leans toward realism: stealth, deliberate aiming, weapon jams, reloads and scarce ammo. He admits it is the game on the list he played least, but respects how it breaks from the usual fast, spray-and-pray shooter formula. The guns, with their many modifiers and upgrades, carry most of the roguelike depth. Repetitive levels, overwhelming detail and a slow unlock system hold it back for him, though the gunplay feels great. He ends by placing it 'around here' on the board without naming a tier letter.
praise: Slow, deliberate shooter pacing that differs from typical fast-paced shooter roguelikes
Huge variety of unique guns with modifiers and upgrades, which is where most of the depth lies
Mechanics like jamming, reloading and limited ammo force awareness of build and gun behavior
Precise, satisfying gunplay; headshots feel great
Sound design and VFX are fantastic
Pre-run class choice with distinct mechanics and different starting weapons
criticism: Levels are repetitive and feel like one big room, reducing immersion
So much detail and complexity that bosses can kill him with no clear cause
Unlocking classes and starting weapons is slow, so runs begin with the same setup
Leveling is per class, so trying another class means starting from zero
unique_points: Approaches the shooter genre realistically and slowly, rewarding stealth and careful aim instead of constant firing
Gun mechanics (jams, reloads, scarce bullets) are central to the roguelike build rather than a side detail
commentary.quote: it really is a very slow pace action rogike
design_criteria: Gameplay depth: complex gun mechanics and a slow pace are what make it distinct
Build variety: many unique guns with modifiers and upgrades drive the roguelike layer
Level design: repetitive, big-room feel counts against it
Readability: dense stats and details make boss deaths hard to understand
Meta-progression: class-locked leveling and slow unlocks limit starting variety
Audio/VFX: sound design and effects make shooting feel great

community.one_liner: A top-down tactical shooter roguelite from Flow Fire Games where hands-on gun handling (active reload, jams, recoil, ammo types) meets randomized weapons, eight classes and a punishing five-floor run against the Machine Legion.
community.consensus_summary: Players love it: Steam shows Very Positive at roughly 94% of about 13,000 reviews, with many reviewers logging hundreds of hours and calling the gunplay among the best in the genre. Critics are few but favourable; Metacritic has only three critic reviews (84, 80, 70 per Wikipedia) and no Metascore yet, plus a user score of 8.1 from 32 ratings. It is a finished, fully released 2018 game (originally Synthetik, renamed Legion Rising after a free October 2018 expansion) with a free spin-off, Synthetik: Arena, and console ports on Xbox and Switch in 2020. A sequel, Synthetik 2, has been in Early Access since 2021. The core complaint is a steep, poorly explained learning curve plus heavy RNG, and some players report crashes and glitches in recent years.
best_things: Gunplay feel: active reload, magazine ejecting, jams/overheating and recoil make every gun feel physical and skill-dependent
Huge weapon pool (70+ guns with manufacturer variants and randomized stats) plus 140+ items (turrets, mines, mind control, orbital lasers) enabling very different builds
Eight classes/subclasses with long progression and prestige arcs, so new unlocks keep coming 30-40+ hours in
Very high replayability and skill ceiling; runs feel like mastery of a build rather than a fixed meta
Sound design and soundtrack are repeatedly called out as excellent
Modular difficulty (about 11 independent modifiers) lets players tune the challenge, including 220%+ for veterans
Two-player online co-op with shared loot is described as great fun by those who get it working
Cheap price for the depth, and a free Arena version works as a demo
worst_things: Poor onboarding: the game drops you into a run with a weak tutorial and items/weapons/mods whose effects are not explained, so reviewers say many mechanics must be discovered or looked up
Harsh RNG can starve a run of weapon crates or upgrade shops for several floors, and runs can end from a single small mistake
Crashes and game-ending bugs, including runs wiped by crashes and getting stuck on obstacles; co-op lobbies sometimes fail to connect
Unfinished or broken interactions (for example the Modular weapon mod is reported as unusable)
Display and UI problems: no real ultrawide or multi-monitor support, minimalistic UI that some find awkward, no item descriptions in shops
Late game spikes hard: floors 4-5, back-to-back gauntlet rooms and the final boss Armageddon are seen as a DPS check that only a handful of weapons can handle
Some features feel gated (a loadout tied to a friend referral code, locked DLC content) which irritated a few reviewers
improvements: A proper tutorial and in-game tooltips/item descriptions, including in shops
Stability fixes for crashes and run-ending bugs, and more reliable co-op lobby/connection
Better balance across the weapon pool so more than a small subset is viable into floors 4-5 and the final boss
Less punishing or more forgiving RNG for crate and upgrade-shop spawns
Display options: ultrawide/multi-monitor support, an earlier settings menu, and a way to disable screen flash
Finish or fix half-implemented content such as the Modular mod
unique_things: Hands-on gun mechanics in a roguelite: manual magazine eject, timed active reload, jams and overheating
Weapons generate with manufacturer-specific variants and randomized stats instead of fixed items
Eight specialist classes that change playstyle entirely, from sneaking assassin to turret engineer to heavy breacher
Engineer-style gambling dynamics (double or nothing with credits) and devil-offer red crates that trade health for power
Modular difficulty sliders and a prestige system rather than a single fixed difficulty
Free companion game Synthetik: Arena shares character and achievement unlocks with the main game
tedious_or_disliked: Long losing streaks while learning: only a small share of players beat the final encounter (one reviewer cites about 7% with the achievement)
Trial-and-error discovery of what items and weapons do, often costing a whole run
Late-floor gauntlets (three hard rooms in a row) and the final boss feel like a slog after a long run
Overwhelming enemy spam and explosive threats such as Doombots in solo play
Grinding class levels and unlocks, and repeating the long runs (8-hour sessions reported)
Screen flash on explosions with no option to turn it off
divisive_points: RNG: fans see it as brutal but fair chaos that creates stories; detractors call it unfair and run-deciding
Difficulty: some treat it as a mastery game and eventually love it, while others bounce within an hour or two
Solo vs co-op: co-op is praised but some find the game too complex or enemy-heavy for a casual co-op session
Synthetik 1 vs 2: at least one 870-hour reviewer says neither the Early Access sequel nor any other game grabbed them like the original
community.reception_notes: Launched March 2018 on Steam and became a large word-of-mouth hit, with multiple Steam reviewers crediting YouTuber Sseth's video for discovering it and one claiming it boosted sales dramatically. A free expansion in October 2018 renamed it Legion Rising. Synthetik: Arena (free, combat-focused) followed in January 2019, and Xbox and Switch versions in December 2020; console reviews noted control and interface issues. Synthetik 2 entered Early Access in 2021. Estimated revenue is about $1.78M gross and about $525k net (Boxleiter-style estimate from steam-revenue-calculator.com, order of magnitude only); SteamSpy-style owner estimate is 500k-1M. PC only on Steam (no Mac/Linux). Recent Steam reviews from 2025-2026 are still strongly positive, though a few report worsening crashes and glitches. Note: web search budget was exhausted in this session, so Reddit and OpenCritic could not be checked; OpenCritic score is unknown, not confirmed absent.
